findings.title: Anonymous early animation branches

chronology.event: NicoNico video sm38852466 republishes an early Shonbori/Tanuki animation and explicitly names Futaba as its repost source; uploader 三代目コペルニクス君 is not treated as the animator.
NicoNico video sm39422705 uses the already-developed Umaru-meeting motion branch; its description says the materials were already fully available.

findings.lineage_summary: Community history describes the first low-frame flailing animation as volunteer-made at Futaba, then records multiple movements traced from the Umaru meeting scene.
findings.community_distribution_context: Historical community commentary describes taking the works outside the community as disfavoured and later diffusion as tacitly tolerated. This is contextual evidence, not an individual licence and not a verified prohibition by a specific local-asset author.
findings.recommended_action: Recover source frames or source packs before linking any local action group; do not credit early NicoNico uploaders as animators when their own descriptions identify the upload as a repost.

evidence.basis: Community history distinguishes an early low-frame hands-and-feet flailing animation from later motions traced from the Himouto! Umaru-chan meeting scene.
Contemporary editorial history describes the flailing GIF, later variants, and dance-video usage, and includes a direct mini-interview with Deon.

A downstream 2024 Tanuki video creator explicitly distinguishes Jitabata from Umaru Dance, describes Umaru Dance as a bow-legged dance, and states that its reusable cycle has eight frames. This supports branch semantics and frame-count compatibility only; the writer is not treated as the template author.

findings.interpretation: All 89 reviewed files can be rejected as motion-semantic matches to the documented canonical Jitabata branch. For the later Umaru-meeting branch, 15 idle_mix_dance* files remain medium-confidence motion candidates: they are broad dance cycles and all have eight frames, matching a downstream creator's description of the reusable Umaru Dance cycle. Another 22 idle_sit_no/wave* files remain low-confidence candidates; 52 are semantic rejections. None of these statuses identifies an author or proves pixel lineage.
findings.limits: Historical source frames were not recovered: early Futaba attachment payloads are unavailable and the in-app browser safety policy blocked the NicoNico player page. Therefore no exact pixel/source-frame match or exclusion is asserted.
findings.recommended_action: Prioritize source-pack or archived-frame recovery for the 15 medium candidates, then the 22 low candidates. Keep every candidate orange until creator identity and reuse/redistribution terms are resolved.

findings.title: Bilibili retrospective video claims and unverified early-creator leads

claims.claim: Deon's 2021-05-19 Shonbori Rudolf image is the visual starting point and later spread to Futaba.
claims.basis: Consistent with the first-party Deon post, the 2021 Inside Games interview, and the 2021-05-31 Futaba archive.

claims.claim: An artist called Rotas made the first hands-and-feet-flailing GIF from Deon's image.
claims.basis: The video visibly names Rotas. Older sources corroborate an anonymous volunteer animation but do not supply that name, account, original post, or policy.

claims.claim: An anonymous creator called the ramen-loving Tanuki friend or Ramen creator began a 2021-09-09 Umaru-derived series and supplied blank-face and component templates.
claims.basis: The video provides the label and date; MUGENwiki supports the Umaru-meeting-derived branch generally but not the claimed identity, profession, or exact date.

claims.claim: Unauthorized reposting and hostile material led to attacks and deletion of the WIKIWIKI asset collection.
claims.basis: The video shows the missing WIKIWIKI page and a later 2022 transport article that mentions deletion, but no first-party administrator statement was recovered.

claims.claim: Many creators tacitly tolerated compilation uploads to video sites.
claims.basis: Consistent with MUGENwiki's explicit description of tacit toleration. Tacit toleration is not an app, repository, source-file, or installer redistribution licence.

claims.claim: The video author acted as a transporter and compiled the Large Tanuki Pack from about 500 to more than 30,000 files.
claims.basis: The video displays a folder property panel with 30,194 files and 1,803 folders; no per-file creator or permission manifest is shown.

findings.limits: Neither Rotas nor the ramen-associated creator has a verified first-party account, original post, policy statement, or exact match to a local GIF. Rotas must not be conflated with the later on-screen name Roterszeng without independent identity evidence.
findings.interpretation: The video materially improves the historical lead list but establishes no new permission for the 456 local GIFs and no asset-specific creator match.
findings.recommended_action: Search the May-June 2021 window for Rotas with Deon and Jitabata terms, and the 2021-09-09 window for the ramen-associated creator with Umaru, blank-face, and component-template terms. Keep all 456 assets orange.

findings.title: 2022-01-19 first-person source thread and recovered animation variants
findings.identity_scope: Opening poster and same public ID in this thread only; no cross-thread or real-world identity inference.

corroborates_video.claim: blank-face variants, expression parts, Rudolf variants and daily-posting hiatus

screening.method: Per-frame alpha bbox crop; zero invisible RGB; hash dimensions plus exact RGBA. Sequence comparison permits cyclic start rotation, records timing separately. No rescale/mirror/fuzzy match in exact results.

findings.permission_finding: No explicit opening-poster prohibition or applicable reuse/redistribution grant identified in this recovered thread. Third-party requests, isolated disputes and favourable comments are not creator terms.
